name: Expulsion of Jews from England
summary: Edward I of England issues the Edict of Expulsion (July 18, 1290), ordering all Jews out of England by November 1. Approximately 2,000–3,000 Jews are expelled, having been systematically stripped of their economic function over the preceding century through anti-usury legislation, forced conversions, and confiscation of debts owed to Jewish creditors. The expulsion follows by 12 years the French expulsion of 1278 and precedes by two years a French mass expulsion. England remained without a recognized Jewish community for 356 years, until Cromwell's tacit readmission (1656).

_quarry.structural_significance: First major national expulsion of Jews in medieval Europe; establishes the template for subsequent French and Iberian expulsions; England's Jewish community is not formally readmitted until 1656, the longest such gap in northern Europe
